title: Generic fibre dimension persists on a nonempty open
statement: Let $f:X\to Y$ be a morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme]. Assume the underlying space of $Y$ is irreducible (nonempty and not the union of two proper closed subsets) with generic point $\eta$ [def-sc-generic-point], and that $f$ is of finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. If the scheme-theoretic generic fibre $X_{\eta}$ [def-pc-scheme-fibre] has topological Krull dimension [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension] $n\ge0$, then there exists a nonempty open subset $V\subseteq Y$ such that every fibre $X_y$ for $y\in V$ has topological Krull dimension exactly $n$.

source.place: More on Morphisms, Lemma Tag 05F7 (lemma-dimension-in-neighbourhood), statement and proof lines 8411–8432; tag verified in literature/stacks-project/tags/tags

proof.text: Let $Z=\{x\in X\mid \dim_x(X_{f(x)})>n\}$. By [lem-weil-pbc-local-fibre-dimension-open], the locus where the local fibre dimension is at most $n$ is open, so $Z$ is closed. The hypothesis $\dim X_\eta=n$ implies that the generic fibre contains no point of $Z$, hence $Z\cap f^{-1}(\{\eta\})=\emptyset$. Finite type gives a locally finite type, quasi-compact morphism by [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Apply [lem-sbc-generic-fibre-closed-avoidance] with $y=\eta$ and $C=Z$. Since $\eta$ is generic in the irreducible space $Y$, $\overline{\{\eta\}}=Y$, so after replacing the resulting open by a nonempty open $V_1$ containing $\eta$, every fibre over $V_1$ is disjoint from $Z$. Its local dimensions are all at most $n$, so [lem-weil-pbc-dimension-supremum-local-dimensions] gives dimension at most $n$ (also for an empty fibre).

source.place: More on Morphisms, Lemma Tag 05F7, proof lines 8417--8422: define the closed locus of local fibre dimension greater than n and remove it after applying Lemma 054W

proof.text: If $n=0$, the generic fibre is nonempty (the empty scheme has dimension below every nonnegative integer), so apply [lem-sbc-generic-closed-subset-fibre-nonempty] to the closed subset $C=X$ and obtain a nonempty open $V_2$ containing $\eta$ over which every fibre is nonempty. If $n>0$, let $Z'=\{x\in X\mid \dim_x(X_{f(x)})>n-1\}$. This is closed because it is the complement of the open bounded-dimension locus for $n-1$. By [lem-weil-pbc-dimension-supremum-local-dimensions], the supremum of the local dimensions of $X_\eta$ is $n$. All are at most $n$; if none equalled $n$, all would be at most $n-1$, contradicting that supremum. Thus some point has local fibre dimension $n$, so $Z'\cap f^{-1}(\{\eta\})$ is nonempty. Apply [lem-sbc-generic-closed-subset-fibre-nonempty] to $Z'$ to obtain a nonempty open $V_2$ containing $\eta$ such that every fibre over $V_2$ meets $Z'$.

source.place: More on Morphisms, Lemma Tag 05F7, proof lines 8423--8429: form the closed locus of local fibre dimension greater than n-1, note that its generic fibre is nonempty, and apply Lemma 05F5 (lemma-nonempty-generic-fibre)

proof.text: Put $V=V_1\cap V_2$. It is a nonempty open containing $\eta$. For $y\in V$, Step 1 gives $\dim X_y\le n$. If $n=0$, Step 2 gives that $X_y$ is nonempty, so its dimension is at least $0$ and hence equals $0$. If $n>0$, Step 2 gives a point of $X_y$ whose local fibre dimension is greater than $n-1$; this local dimension is at most $n$ by Step 1, so it is a finite integer and is at least $n$. The dimension of the fibre is at least every local dimension, hence is at least $n$, and therefore equals $n$ by the upper bound. The same argument covers all points of $V$ and proves the claim.
